about: The droids' voices, made from formants as each line is spoken: see src/formants/speech.rs. 'phones' are the sounds of speech, one per letter as System Latin reads it (j is the y of 'iam', w the u of 'qu'): where the three formants sit, in Hz, how long it lasts, in seconds, how much buzz (voice) and noise (hiss) it is made of, and how loud it is. A 'stop' is a moment's silence and then a burst of its noise; a voiced one murmurs while it is closed. 'widths' is how wide each of the three formants is, in Hz, and 'gains' how loud. 'pauses' are the gaps between words, at a comma and at the end of a sentence, in seconds. 'voices' are each kind of droid's voice, by the name it has in data/dialogue/droids.json, with 'default' for any other: its 'pitch' in Hz, its 'speed' (2 is twice as fast), its 'size' (every formant is this many times as high, so under 1 sounds bigger), how far each vowel's note steps up or down ('lilt'), how far a sentence falls over its length ('fall') and a question rises at its end ('rise'), each as a part of the pitch, how much hiss goes along with its voice ('breath'), how loud it is at its loudest ('volume', from 0 to 1), and how far off, in meters, it is heard at full volume ('reach'). Each droid speaks a little higher or lower than the rest of its kind. 'moods' is how many times its usual pitch a droid speaks at in each mood a line can have (see data/dialogue/droids.json): higher when pleased, questioning or agitated, lower when hostile; any not given is 1.
